summary: The narrator wakes at dawn in a stone room atop a Mayan-style pyramid at Baalum, after a stormy night spent waiting for Sarah, who he is certain was nearby. He had resolved to rest, keep watch on the plaza, and search for her at first light, but he drifts into a dreamless sleep. At dawn he sees the cobalt sky, mist below the pyramid, and glyphs and bas-reliefs on the walls, then resolves to go to the Rio Tigre, the only thing he knows Sarah touched, and see it in daylight.
one_line: At dawn on a Mayan pyramid at Baalum, the narrator wakes after a stormy night, resolving to search for Sarah and visit the Rio Tigre.
key_facts: The narrator is certain Sarah was somewhere out in the rain, and he feels her presence like a sixth sense.
He decides that plunging into the storm to look for her would be the stupidest thing he could do.
His plan is to rest until the storm clears, keep periodic watch on the plaza, and search for Sarah as soon as there is light.
He drifts off into a dreamless doze, lulled by the wind in the giant Cebia trees and forest rain drumming on the roof.
He wakes when a sliver of sun flashes through the stone doorway and forest birds erupt in celebration.
The dawn sky is described as the purest blue he has ever seen, a swath of artist's cobalt.
Below the pyramid, a bank of dense, pastel mist hides the plaza, so the top of the pyramid seems to float on a cloud.
Sarah had called this place 'Babylon,' which the narrator notes as ancient and mysterious.
The room's inside walls are embossed with rows of classic Mayan glyphs molded in newly set plaster.
Raised bas-reliefs of warriors in battle dress sit beside the glyphs in the room.
The narrator rolls his sleeping bag and stuffs his still-moist clothes into his backpack.
The river is the Rio Tigre, located at the back of the pyramid.
The Rio Tigre was Sarah's way out and the only thing the narrator knows for sure she touched.
The narrator's pulse rises as he resolves to see the river in the light of day and heads through the rear door.

entities.name: Sarah
entities.role: the woman the narrator is searching for; she called the place 'Babylon' and is believed to have returned to Baalum after someone tried to murder her

entities.name: Baalum
entities.role: the ancient Mayan-style site with a pyramid where the narrator spends the night and to which Sarah may have returned

entities.name: Rio Tigre
entities.role: river at the back of the pyramid that served as Sarah's way out

entities.name: Cebia trees
entities.role: giant trees in the rain forest whose wind sounds lull the narrator to sleep

entities.name: Bell
entities.role: vehicle the narrator traveled in, described as a teeth-rattling trip
